title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Playbook
author: Priya Shah
content:
Summary:
This playbook codifies Redwood Inference's People Operations approach for hiring, pre-boarding, onboarding, the performance and feedback cycle, and manager responsibilities. It is intended for People Ops partners, hiring managers, interviewers, and new hires. Use this as the canonical reference for process, templates, SLAs, and checklists.

Scope:
- Applies to all full-time employees (FTE), contractors engaged for >6 months, and internal transfers.
- Includes technical and non-technical hiring, remote-first and on-site candidates, and both US and international hires.

Owner & contacts:
- Playbook owner: Priya Shah (People Ops) — priya@redwood.ai
- Escalation: People Ops lead (people-ops@redwood.ai)
- Hiring system: Lever (recruiting), Greenhouse (backup), Workday (HR records)

Key targets (SLAs / goals):
- Time-to-offer (requisition approved -> offer sent): 28 days target
- Offer acceptance rate: >= 75%
- Candidate NPS (post-process survey): >= 60
- New-hire time-to-productivity (baseline): 90 days

1) Hiring process (end-to-end)
Purpose: deliver high-quality hires fairly and efficiently while providing an excellent candidate experience.

1.1 Requisition & role definition
- Hiring manager creates a requisition in Lever and completes the "Role Definition" template. Required fields: team mission, specific outcomes for first 6 months, required vs. preferred skills, salary band, hiring committee members, remote/location constraints.
- People Ops reviews and posts job within 2 business days.

1.2 Sourcing & outreach
- Recruiter owns active sourcing pipelines and coordinates with hiring manager weekly.
- Diversity sourcing targets: aim for at least 30% of the candidate slate to be underrepresented-group candidates when feasible; record outreach metrics in Lever.

1.3 Interview loop and rubrics
- Standard interview loop (example for engineers): Recruiter screen -> Hiring manager screen -> Technical assessment (take-home or coding exercise) -> On-site / virtual loop (4 interviews: system design, coding, product/behavioral, culture) -> Hiring committee review -> Offer.
- Required documentation: Interview plan (roles, outcomes), candidate evaluation rubric (technical, communication, ownership, culture add).
- Scoring: Use a 1-5 scale per dimension. Interviewers must submit written notes for scores <=2 or >=5. No single interviewer veto without documented rationale and discussion during committee review.

Interview rubric (example fields):
- Technical competence
- Problem decomposition & clarity
- Product sense (where relevant)
- Communication & collaboration
- Ownership & delivery
- Hiring bar (yes/no)

1.4 Decision & offer
- Hiring manager and recruiter draft compensation within established band, consult with People Ops compensation specialist for exceptions.
- Offer approval flow: Manager -> Director -> People Ops -> Finance (if offer is above band). Target turnaround: 48 business hours.
- Offer letter contents: start date, role, band, equity grant outline, manager name, relocation/visa notes (if applicable), basic benefits summary.

1.5 Post-offer process
- Acceptances recorded in HRIS within 24 hours. Pre-boarding checklist triggered: IT ticket, equipment procurement, calendar invites for orientation and first-week meetings, benefits enrollment instructions.

2) Pre-boarding & Onboarding
Objective: reduce time-to-productivity and increase new-hire engagement during the first 90 days.

2.1 Pre-boarding (prior to start date)
- People Ops sends welcome packet: benefits overview, first-week agenda, handbook links, required paperwork, and manager contact.
- Manager actions (to complete before day 1): team announcement, publish first 30 days plan, assign onboarding project (small meaningful task), create calendar invites for core recurring meetings.
- IT actions: laptop imaged and shipped (remote) 5 business days before start or available on day 1; account access requests (Slack, email, internal tools) submitted with standard role templates.

2.2 Day 1 agenda (example)
- 09:00 — Orientation (People Ops): company mission, org chart, benefits walk-through
- 10:30 — Manager welcome & role review
- 11:30 — Lunch with buddy
- 13:00 — Workspace & tools setup (IT)
- 15:00 — First 1:1: expectations and 30/60/90 plan

2.3 First-week checklist (manager)
- Introductions to cross-functional partners
- Assign onboarding buddy (peer) and schedule recurring touchpoints
- Deliver onboarding project brief and success criteria
- Schedule role-specific training sessions and knowledge transfer meetings
- Ensure required compliance trainings are assigned in LMS and completion tracked

2.4 30-60-90 day plan (template)
- 30 days: Understand product, codebase, tools, and processes; complete onboarding project; attend key team rituals.
- 60 days: Own a small production task, contribute to design discussions, demonstrate reliable execution.
- 90 days: Independently deliver on agreed outcomes; meet with manager for calibration and next objectives.

3) Performance & feedback cycles
Goal: create continuous feedback loops, fair calibration, and clear career growth pathways.

3.1 Continuous feedback & 1:1s
- Managers should hold weekly or bi-weekly 1:1s depending on team cadence. Use shared meeting notes (Confluence template) and track action items.
- Encourage asynchronous feedback via peer-recognition tools and mid-sprint checkpoints.

3.2 Mid-year and year-end reviews
- Cycle cadence: Mid-year check-in (June), Year-end review (December). Templates and calendar invites are published in People Ops Confluence.
- Review components: self-assessment, manager assessment, peer feedback, and manager calibration meeting.
- Rating scale: Exceeds Expectations / Meets Expectations / Needs Development. Written feedback required for "Needs Development" and "Exceeds Expectations" ratings.

3.3 Calibration & promotions
- Calibration meetings include managers, directors, and People Ops to align ratings and bands. Evidence-based discussion required.
- Promotion packet requirements: updated role profile, manager narrative, three examples of impact, peer/partner feedback, recommended band/level change. People Ops policy review and decision published within 4 weeks of submission.

3.4 Performance Improvement Plans (PIP)
- PIP is used when sustained performance gaps exist after coaching (generally following >= 60 days of documented concerns). Steps: documented objectives, measurable success criteria, manager support plan, HR oversight, and 30/60/90 day checkpoints. People Ops must be engaged before issuing a formal PIP.

4) People policies & guidelines
4.1 Probation & confirmation
- Most new FTEs have a 90-day probationary period. Confirmation requires manager sign-off and People Ops verification of completion of onboarding milestones.

4.2 Time off & remote work
- PTO policy: follow company handbook (link). Managers approve PTO requests in HRIS; requests >5 business days should be submitted at least 2 weeks in advance.
- Remote-first policy: flexible work arrangements are supported; teams should set core overlap hours (recommended 10:00–16:00 local) to support collaboration.

4.3 Compensation & equity overview
- Compensation bands are maintained by People Ops in partnership with Finance. Managers consult People Ops for off-band offers or counter-offers. Equity grants are determined by level and hiring cycle; specific guidance is in the compensation policy.

5) Manager guide: best practices and checklists
5.1 First 30 days as a manager of a new hire
- Day 0: Announce new hire to team with role context, start date, and first-week plan.
- Day 1–7: Run onboarding kickoff, assign buddy, review 30/60/90 plan, and confirm access.
- Week 2–4: Deliver early feedback conversation; set immediate objectives; connect new hire with cross-functional partners.

5.2 Running effective 1:1s (template)
- 1) Quick check-in (2–5 min)
- 2) Wins & highlights (5–10 min)
- 3) Blockers & support (10–15 min)
- 4) Career & development (10 min)
- 5) Action items & priorities (5 min)

5.3 Difficult conversations and offboarding
- Prepare: document examples, prior coaching, and involve People Ops early for guidance.
- Process: manager consults People Ops -> legal (if required) -> separation decision. Conduct exit conversations with compassion, clarity on next steps, and provide separation resources per policy.

6) Templates & checklists (references)
6.1 Interview feedback template (Confluence link)
- Candidate name:

- Written strengths/risks and hire recommendation
